topic: Newton's Third Law
hook: Stop saying 'Every action has an equal and opposite reaction'—you're losing 4 marks in JEE/NEET right now!
body: Think of a classic thappad: the instant your hand strikes a cheek, the cheek exerts the EXACT same force on your hand at the EXACT same millisecond. Forces always exist in simultaneous pairs—neither force is the 'cause' or 'effect'.
trap: 90% of students think action-reaction forces cancel each other out to zero. Big mistake! They act on TWO DIFFERENT bodies (Hand on Face vs. Face on Hand), so they can NEVER cancel out.
win: Master rule: If forces act on the same object, it's equilibrium; if on different objects, it's a Newton's 3rd law pair. Lock those +4 marks!

topic: Trigonometry Basics
hook: Stop memorizing trigonometry tables blindly! If you keep messing up sin, cos, and tan in exams, look at this one simple trick.
body: Think of a right-angled triangle like climbing a flyover. The ramp is the Hypotenuse—always the longest side. The pillar standing right opposite to your angle θ is Perpendicular, and the ground underneath is Base. Just remember: 'Pandit Badri Prasad, Har Har Bole'—P/H is Sin, B/H is Cos, and P/B is Tan!
trap: 90% of students assume the vertical side is always Perpendicular. Trap alert: Perpendicular is ALWAYS the side directly opposite to your chosen angle θ, which flips if you switch angles!
win: Lock this orientation rule down and you will never lose those guaranteed 4 to 6 marks in your board or entrance exams.

topic: Chemical Bonding
hook: Stop memorizing bond orders blindly! Why do atoms even bother to bond in the first place?
body: Think of atoms like guests at an Indian wedding: high energy means utter chaos and instability. To achieve true 'sukoon' (lowest potential energy state), they either share paneer (covalent bonding via electron sharing) or transfer the whole mithai box (ionic bonding via electron transfer) just to complete their stable octet.
trap: 90% of students blindly assume ionic compounds always have higher melting points than covalent ones, completely forgetting giant network covalent solids like diamond and quartz!
win: Remember the golden rule: stability equals minimum potential energy. Lock in an easy 4 marks in JEE and NEET!

topic: Probability Basics
hook: Stop scrolling! If a coin lands Heads 5 times in a row, is Tails guaranteed next? 99% of students get this wrong!
body: Probability is just: Favourable Outcomes divided by Total Outcomes. Imagine a sweet box with 4 Kaju Katlis and 6 Gulab Jamuns—total 10 sweets. The probability of picking a Kaju Katli blindly is 4 out of 10, or 2/5 (40%). Simple fraction, zero magic!
trap: The Gambler's Trap: Believing past coin flips force the next outcome. A coin has no memory—each flip is an independent event with exactly 1/2 probability!
win: Remember: Probability always lies between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain). Lock this down and secure easy guaranteed marks in your exams!

topic: Indian Constitution Preamble

It declares the source ('We, the People') and sets India's identity as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic aiming to secure Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity for all.
trap: 90% of aspirants lose marks forgetting that 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' were NOT in the original 1949 Constitution—they were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976! Also remember, the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution, but it is non-justiciable.
win: Master the 42nd Amendment additions and the Kesavananda Bharati case to lock in 2 guaranteed marks in your next exam.

topic: Law Clat Ailet Judiciary
hook: Did you know you can win a lawsuit in court even if you suffered zero financial loss?
body: CLAT and Judiciary exams constantly test 'Injuria Sine Damno' versus 'Damnum Sine Injuria'. Think of your local chai tapri: if a rival stall opens next door and cuts your daily profit in half, you lost money, but no legal right was infringed—that is Damnum Sine Injuria, zero compensation! But if someone wrongfully prevents you from casting your vote, you lost zero rupees, yet your legal right was violated—that is Injuria Sine Damno, and you win damages in court.
trap: 90% of students assume liability exists simply because financial damage occurred, forgetting that mere monetary loss without a legal violation is not actionable in tort law.
win: Always check the legal right first: no legal injury equals no compensation, no matter how large the financial loss!

topic: Railway RRB Ntpc Alp Je Groupd
hook: Train wale questions mein har baar negative marks? Yeh 3-second rule dekho!
body: Jab train kisi platform ya tunnel ko cross karti hai, toh total distance sirf platform ki nahi, balki Train + Platform dono ki hoti hai. Jaise chai banate waqt sirf doodh nahi, paani aur doodh dono ka volume judta hai: Total Distance = (Train Length + Platform Length). Aur speed km/h se m/s karne ke liye bas 5/18 se multiply karo.
trap: 90% aspirants train ki apni length add karna bhool jate hain aur sirf platform ki length use karke negative marking le aate hain.
win: Yaad rakho: Agar samne wali cheez ki length hai, toh dono add honge. Ek concept, aur RRB NTPC, ALP ya Group D mein pakka 1 mark secure!

topic: Carnot Cycle Micro-Concept 1.2 (Chapter 2.1: Core Applications of Carnot Cycle)
hook: Stop memorizing Carnot efficiency formulas blindly—you are losing easy marks!
body: Think of the Carnot cycle as the 'Sharma ji ka beta' of thermodynamics: it represents the ultimate benchmark that no real heat engine or refrigerator can ever beat between two fixed temperatures. Whether it's a power plant or an AC, Carnot proves that maximum efficiency depends strictly on reservoir temperatures, never on the working substance.
trap: 90% of students plug temperatures in Celsius instead of Kelvin, or assume using exotic fuels can beat Carnot limit!
win: Free 4 marks: Always convert to Kelvin first and remember η depends solely on T_hot and T_cold!

topic: Number Theory Diophantine Equations Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 1.2: Core Applications of Number Theory Diophantine Equations)
hook: Can you pay exactly 43 rupees using only 6-rupee and 9-rupee coupons? Stop guessing—it is mathematically impossible!
body: For any Linear Diophantine Equation ax + by = c to have integer solutions, GCD(a, b) must divide c. Think of it like a local kirana store: if your coin denominations are 6 and 9, their greatest common factor is 3, meaning you can only ever form bill amounts that are exact multiples of 3. Since 3 does not divide 43, no combination of integer coupons will ever work.
trap: 90% of students immediately start rearranging terms and testing random integer values, wasting critical exam minutes on equations that have zero integer solutions.
win: Always compute GCD(a, b) first. If it does not divide c, instantly mark 'No Integer Solution' and bank free marks in under 5 seconds.

topic: Enzyme Kinetics Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 1.2: Core Applications of Enzyme Kinetics)
hook: Stop memorizing Lineweaver-Burk plots until you understand how doctors use enzyme kinetics to literally reverse poison!
body: Here is a core application: competitive inhibition in medicine. Imagine an enzyme is a busy Mumbai local train door and substrate is the passenger. If toxic methanol enters your body, doctors flood your system with ethanol. Ethanol competes for Alcohol Dehydrogenase, blocking the toxic breakdown just like crowd management, buying time to flush it out safely!
trap: 90% of students write that competitive inhibitors decrease Vmax. Total trap! High substrate concentration easily overcomes the inhibitor, so Vmax stays constant—only apparent Km increases.
win: Remember: Competitive inhibitor = Km increases, Vmax remains unchanged. That is 4 free marks in your exam!

topic: Evidence Act Micro-Concept 1.2 (Chapter 2.1: Core Applications of Evidence Act)
hook: Stop writing affidavits thinking the Evidence Act applies to them! 90% of students lose free marks here.
body: The Evidence Act is like a strict board exam invigilator—it only supervises full judicial proceedings in court. Just like street gully cricket doesn't follow ICC umpire DRS rules, the Evidence Act strictly does NOT apply to arbitration proceedings or court affidavits (Section 1).
trap: Marking 'Applies to all legal proceedings' in prelims. Remember: Arbitration and Affidavits are completely OUTSIDE the Evidence Act.
win: Remember the rule of 'Double A' (Affidavits & Arbitration = No Evidence Act) and secure an instant 2 marks in your next Judiciary or CLAT exam!

topic: Permutations Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Permutations)
hook: Stop using the nPr formula blindly in JEE and CAT until you check this one condition!
body: Think of permutations like reserving specific window seats on an IRCTC train. If 3 friends sit on berths 21, 22, and 23, Rahul on the window is completely different from Rohan on the window. Whenever the sequence or position changes the outcome, that is a permutation—just fill the slots sequentially: 3 × 2 × 1.
trap: Confusing arrangement with selection! 90% of students use nPr when picking a 3-person project team, forgetting that Rahul-Rohan-Aman is the exact same team as Aman-Rohan-Rahul.
win: Remember the golden check: 'Position or rank matters? Permute. Just grouping together? Combine.' Never lose these 4 easy marks again!

topic: Formative Assessment Micro-Concept 1.1 (Chapter 1.1: Core Applications of Formative Assessment)
hook: Stop judging your mock tests like they're the final board exam!
body: Formative assessment isn't a final verdict—it's like tasting the dal while cooking so you can adjust the salt before serving guests. Its core application is diagnosing learning gaps in real time through quick chapter quizzes and self-check questions, letting you fix confusion while studying rather than after failing.
trap: 90% of students fixate purely on the score and feel demotivated instead of analyzing which specific concept caused the error.
win: Treat every mini-quiz as a diagnostic tool: pinpoint one concept gap, fix it immediately, and lock in extra marks for exam day.

topic: Multi-Head Latent Attention Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Multi-Head Latent Attention)
hook: Stop scrolling if you're prepping for AI exams! This one attention trick saves 90% of GPU memory in modern LLMs.
body: Standard Multi-Head Attention stores massive KV caches—like every passenger dragging three giant steel trunks into a packed Mumbai local train, causing an instant jam! MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention) acts like a centralized parcel service: it compresses Key and Value vectors into a single tiny low-dimensional latent space before storing in VRAM, only projecting them back up during computation. This allows massive context windows and giant batch sizes with minimal memory overhead.
trap: 90% of students confuse MLA with Multi-Query or Grouped-Query Attention. MQA/GQA simply forces heads to share keys, hurting capacity, while MLA uses low-rank latent projection to keep full multi-head expressive power.
win: Remember for your exam: MLA = Low-Rank Latent KV Cache Compression for ultra-efficient long-context inference.

topic: HNSW Indexing Micro-Concept 1.2 (Chapter 1.1: Core Applications of HNSW Indexing)
hook: Stop scanning a billion vectors one by one! If you think production AI search scans entire tables, your ML exam score is in danger.
body: HNSW is the core engine behind ChatGPT's RAG retrieval, Spotify's song recommendations, and e-commerce visual search. Think of it like Indian transport: top layers act like the Vande Bharat Express skipping tiny stations to reach the right city in milliseconds, while bottom layers act like local autos navigating specific gallis to pin down your nearest vector neighbor in O(log N) time.
trap: Confusing HNSW with traditional B-Tree SQL indexing—HNSW is strictly for high-dimensional Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) semantic similarity, never exact keyword lookups or range queries!
win: Formula: Billion-scale items + High dimensions + Sub-millisecond similarity = HNSW. Lock this in for guaranteed marks in ML System Design!

topic: Optimization Techniques Micro-Concept 1.1 (Chapter 2.1: Core Applications of Optimization Techniques)
hook: Stop memorizing optimization formulas! Why does Google Maps choose the longer bypass over the shorter flyover during rush hour?
body: Every real-world optimization boils down to two things: an Objective Function and Constraints. Think of it like ordering food in your college hostel with just ₹200. Your Objective is to maximize calories and taste, but your Constraints are your tight budget and the mess closing in 20 minutes. Whether it is routing network packets in GATE, training machine learning loss functions, or inventory control, optimization is simply finding the best possible outcome without violating your real-world boundaries.
trap: 90% of students confuse the Objective Function with the Constraints—they mistakenly try to directly optimize the constraint parameter instead of optimizing the target performance subject to those limits.
win: Exam Master Rule: Always ask 'What is the goal?' to fix your Objective (e.g., minimize cost or maximize throughput), and 'What is holding me back?' to define your Constraints. Lock this pair first, and optimization formulation MCQs become free marks!

topic: Neural Synaptic Transmission Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Neural Synaptic Transmission)
hook: Stop scrolling! Ever wondered why anesthesia knocks out pain in seconds, but a cup of chai makes your brain race?
body: It all comes down to clinical applications of synaptic transmission! Imagine the synaptic cleft as a busy metro token counter: pre-synaptic neurons release neurotransmitter 'tokens' (like acetylcholine or GABA) that cross the gap to activate post-synaptic receptors. Medicines work by either blocking these counters (like local anesthetics stopping pain signals) or boosting neurotransmitter availability (like anti-depressants inhibiting reuptake).
trap: 90% of NEET aspirants assume all impulses jump across synapses electrically—wrong! In humans, almost all regulatory drugs target chemical synapses, where neurotransmitters act as chemical messengers.
win: Remember: Synapse is a chemical checkpoint, not just a wire! Master receptor agonists and antagonists to lock in +4 marks in Neural Control & Coordination.

topic: Eigenvalues Micro-Concept 1.1 (Chapter 2.1: Core Applications of Eigenvalues)
hook: Stop memorizing det(A - λI) = 0 without understanding what it actually does!
body: Imagine a matrix transformation like a chaotic Mumbai local train—it pushes, stretches, and rotates most vectors in random directions. But Eigenvectors are the VIP passengers: they only get stretched or compressed along their exact same line without changing direction. That scaling factor? That is your Eigenvalue. Google PageRank and bridge resonance calculations all rely on finding these invariant directions.
trap: 90% of students forget that while an Eigenvalue CAN be zero, an Eigenvector can NEVER be the zero vector!
win: Remember: Eigenvalues reveal the axes of pure scaling—lock this concept for an easy 4 marks in GATE and engineering exams!

topic: Burden of Proof Micro-Concept 1.1 (Chapter 1.1: Core Applications of Burden of Proof)
hook: Stop saying 'Prove me wrong'—in Indian courts, that mistake will cost you marks!
body: Section 101 of the Indian Evidence Act lays down: 'He who asserts must prove.' Think of it like a cricket appeal: if you shout 'Howzat' for LBW, the burden is entirely on your team to convince the umpire, not on the batsman to prove innocence.
trap: 90% of students confuse Legal Burden (Section 101, which never shifts from prosecution) with Evidential Burden (Section 102, which shifts back and forth like a badminton shuttlecock).
win: Golden Rule: 'Jo claim karega, wahi prove karega.' Lock this Section 101 vs 102 rule to secure easy marks in CLAT & Judiciary exams!

topic: Thévenin Norton Theorems Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Thévenin Norton Theorems)
hook: Stop solving 5-loop KVL equations! GATE and JEE examiners hide the easiest 2 marks right here.
body: Thévenin and Norton are your circuit's Swiggy delivery. Instead of visiting 10 different kitchen counters (the huge linear network), Thévenin wraps everything across your load resistor RL into ONE battery Vth in series with Rth, and Norton turns it into ONE current source IN in parallel with RN. If the load changes 10 times, you find load current in 2 seconds flat without recalculating the whole messy circuit!
trap: 90% student trap: Deactivating dependent sources like independent ones while finding Rth! Independent sources get shorted or opened, but dependent sources stay alive—apply a 1V test source at load terminals instead.
win: Master the instant bridge: Vth = IN × Rth. Switch between Thévenin and Norton via simple source transformation to crack complex load-variation problems in under 30 seconds!

topic: Argument Logic Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Argument Logic)
hook: Stop solving Critical Reasoning questions like Reading Comprehension—you are bleeding easy marks!
body: The core application of Argument Logic is finding the 'Unstated Assumption'—the invisible bridge between premise and conclusion. Think of it like making cutting chai: your premise is milk and tea leaves, your conclusion is hot chai. The hidden assumption? The gas stove is turned on! If there is no heat, the conclusion collapses.
trap: 90% of aspirants pick an option that merely restates a stated fact from the passage instead of uncovering the author's silent bridge.
win: Apply the Negation Test: negate the option in your head; if it shatters the author's main conclusion, you've locked in +3 marks!

topic: Gauss Law Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Gauss Law)
hook: Stop memorizing 5 different electric field formulas—Gauss Law is just your mom's roti roller!
body: Imagine wrapping a cylindrical steel dabba around an infinite wire with charge density lambda. Electric flux only shoots out through the curved walls, giving E = lambda / (2*pi*eps0*r). For an infinite charged sheet, poke a cylinder through it like a cookie cutter—flux punches out equally from both flat circular caps, giving E = sigma / (2*eps0), totally independent of distance!
trap: 90% of JEE and NEET aspirants forget that while Gauss Law is universally true, you can ONLY pull E out of the integral when the surface has perfect geometric symmetry. Applying it to finite rods will cost you negative marks!
win: Symmetry shortcut: Line -> Cylinder, Sheet -> Pillbox, Point/Shell -> Concentric sphere. Instant 4 marks secured without tedious integration!

topic: Separation of Powers Micro-Concept 2.1 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Separation of Powers)
hook: Wait! Can the Supreme Court actually make laws in India? Think again.
body: Think of it like a cricket match: Parliament is the ICC framing the rules, the Executive is the on-field umpire running the game, and the Judiciary is the third umpire reviewing decisions against the rulebook (the Constitution). Each organ operates on its own pitch to prevent absolute power!
trap: Believing India follows a strict, water-tight separation of powers like the US. In India, the Executive is drawn directly from the Legislature, creating an overlap controlled by checks and balances.
win: Lock this keyword in memory: 'Functional overlap with Checks and Balances'—drop this exact phrase in your Polity answers to lock in top marks!

topic: Formative Assessment Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 1.2: Core Applications of Formative Assessment)
hook: Stop treating mock tests like final board exams! You are destroying your rank before the exam even begins.
body: Core Formative Assessment is 'Assessment FOR Learning'. Think of it like tasting chai while it's boiling on the stove—you check sugar and ginger midway to fix the taste before serving guests. Its main application is real-time feedback and diagnostic correction during the learning process, not giving you a final pass/fail grade!
trap: 90% aspirants check only their percentage score and get depressed, completely ignoring error analysis and immediate remedial practice.
win: Treat every practice quiz like an X-ray to diagnose 2 weak concepts today, fix them tonight, and instantly boost your actual exam score!

topic: Transmission Line Parameters Micro-Concept 1.1 (Chapter 2.1: Core Applications of Transmission Line Parameters)
hook: Stop solving Transmission Line questions like simple Ohm's Law circuits—you are losing easy GATE marks!
body: Think of a 500 km transmission line like a crowded national highway. You don't have all hurdles at one toll plaza; series resistance (R) and inductance (L) are friction distributed every single kilometer along the road, while line-to-ground capacitance (C) and conductance (G) act like tiny continuous side-exits leaking charge and current to ground. They are always distributed per-kilometer parameters, never lumped single components!
trap: 90% of aspirants confuse Shunt Conductance (G) with 1/R! Conductance G models dielectric leakage across insulators and corona loss to ground, NOT the inverse of conductor series resistance.
win: Quick Formula Lock: Series parameters (R, L) oppose line current; Shunt parameters (C, G) govern line voltage and dielectric leakage per unit length.

topic: Lagrangian Mechanics Micro-Concept 1.2 (Chapter 1.1: Core Applications of Lagrangian Mechanics)
hook: Stop drawing 10 messy Free Body Diagrams for connected masses!
body: Lagrangian L = T - V lets you bypass all internal constraint forces like tension and normal reaction. Think of constraint forces like annoying traffic signals on the road—using generalized coordinates with Lagrangian mechanics is like taking the direct metro route: you only track Total Kinetic Energy minus Potential Energy and solve in two simple steps!
trap: 90% of students mess up the velocity terms in polar/spherical coordinates, forgetting the angular kinetic component like r² theta-dot squared, or flipping the sign of V in L = T - V.
win: Master generalized coordinates once, and crack complex coupled systems in 2 clean lines for guaranteed marks in GATE and CSIR NET!

topic: Geometric Transformations Micro-Concept 2.1 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Geometric Transformations)
hook: Stop memorizing 10 different transformation formulas! One mental flip across the diagonal saves you 4 marks instantly.
body: Think of reflection across y = x like flipping an omlette on a tawa: every point (x, y) simply swaps places to become (y, x). When shifting graphs like f(x - a), think of Indian train timings: a delay of '+a' means the curve arrives at the same station later, shifting the entire graph to the right, not left!
trap: 90% of students see f(x + 2) and shift the graph right, confusing the sign inside the function with coordinate addition.
win: Remember 'inside is opposite, outside is direct' to solve any transformation problem in JEE under 20 seconds.

topic: eBPF Tracing Micro-Concept 2.1 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of eBPF Tracing)
hook: Still using heavy APMs and print statements that slow down production servers? Stop right there!
body: eBPF tracing lets you inspect kernel events and user-space apps safely at runtime without changing a single line of code. Think of it like a smart FASTag scanner at a highway toll—it monitors and logs every passing vehicle instantaneously without stopping the traffic!
trap: 90% of students think eBPF recompiles or modifies the Linux kernel source—trap! It runs safely inside a sandboxed JIT verifier with near-zero overhead.
win: For your systems and cloud exam: whenever the question asks for low-overhead, real-time observability in Linux kernel space, choose eBPF!

topic: Number Theory Diophantine Equations Micro-Concept 2.1 (Chapter 1.2: Core Applications of Number Theory Diophantine Equations)
hook: Stop guessing integer solutions! Can you pay exactly ₹47 using only ₹10 notes and ₹15 coins?
body: That is a Linear Diophantine Equation: 10x + 15y = c. By Bézout's identity, integer solutions exist if and only if gcd(a, b) divides c. Think of it like buying chai and samosas: gcd(10, 15) is 5, and since 5 cannot divide 47, no whole note combination will ever pay the bill!
trap: 90% of students jump straight into the Extended Euclidean Algorithm without checking divisibility first, burning 5 minutes on an impossible equation.
win: Always test gcd(a, b) | c first: if it fails, write 'No Integer Solutions' and pocket those 4 marks in 5 seconds flat!

topic: Int8 Product Quantization Micro-Concept 1.1 (Chapter 2.1: Core Applications of Int8 Product Quantization)
hook: Stop storing massive AI embeddings as 32-bit floats before your server runs out of memory!
body: Think of Int8 Product Quantization like a Mumbai Dabbawala coding system. Instead of writing full addresses for 1000 items, you split the vector into small sub-vectors and assign each an 8-bit code from a pre-learned codebook. In vector databases, this compresses high-dimensional vectors by 4x to 8x, slashing RAM costs while powering lightning-fast similarity search for billion-scale RAG and recommendation engines.
trap: Assuming PQ just rounds float32 to int8—that is Scalar Quantization! Product Quantization slices vectors into subspaces and clusters them to preserve relational geometry.
win: Remember: PQ divides vectors, assigns 8-bit centroid IDs, and delivers high recall with up to 90%+ RAM savings—a guaranteed scoring concept for AI/ML systems exams!

topic: Piaget Cognitive Stages Micro-Concept 2.2 (Chapter 1.2: Core Applications of Piaget Cognitive Stages)
hook: Stop teaching algebra to a 7-year-old! You're fighting brain biology, and CTET loves testing this!
body: Piaget's golden application rule: Development precedes learning. If a kid is in the Concrete Operational stage (7 to 11 yrs), they need real objects to learn—like cutting a round roti into equal halves to explain fractions, instead of forcing abstract board formulas.
trap: Mistaking rote lecture for understanding. 90% pick options where teachers give direct definitions, forgetting Piaget viewed kids as 'little scientists' who must actively manipulate concrete material first.
win: Quick exam hack: Match the pedagogy to the stage—Concrete stage gets hands-on tools, Formal stage gets abstract logic. Guaranteed 1 mark locked!

topic: Euclidean Geometry Micro-Concept 2.1 (Chapter 2.2: Core Applications of Euclidean Geometry)
hook: Stop solving 10-line geometry proofs! This one triangle trick saves 2 minutes in JEE and Boards.
body: Think of Thales' Theorem (BPT) like slicing a samosa parallel to the base—the cut always divides both sides in the exact same proportion! If line DE is parallel to base BC in triangle ABC, then AD/DB equals AE/EC every single time.
trap: 90% of students blindly write AD/DB = DE/BC. Huge trap! For parallel bases, you must take the full triangle ratio: AD/AB = DE/BC.
win: Piece-by-piece for sides (AD/DB), full-length for bases (AD/AB). Lock this in and grab a guaranteed +4 marks!
